types.name: 10-K Risk Factors (prose only)
types.summary: 10-K risk factors prose under Reg S-K Item 105 (with annual updates). Only the prose is checked.

checks.name: Risk-factor section heading + introduction
checks.description: Filing must include a clearly labeled 'Risk Factors' section with introduction (Item 105).

checks.name: Item 105 — material-risk-only standard + 15-page summary trigger
checks.description: Risk factors must address material risks only; > 15-page sections require a separate 2-page risk-factor summary.

checks.name: Generic / boilerplate risk factor flagged
checks.description: Risk factors must not be generic boilerplate applicable to any company.

checks.name: Hypothetical / 'could' risk-factor language flagged for specificity
checks.description: Risk factors that hedge as merely hypothetical without specifying current exposures should be flagged.

checks.name: Risk-factor headlines / subheadings (plain English)
checks.description: Each risk factor should have a concise, plain-English headline (Item 105 + Rule 421).

checks.name: Forward-looking statement safe-harbor cross-reference (PSLRA)
checks.description: Risk factors should cross-reference the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act safe harbor where applicable.

checks.name: Cybersecurity / data-breach risk factor
checks.description: Risk factors should address cybersecurity / data-breach risk (per 2023 cybersecurity disclosure rules).

checks.name: Climate / environmental risk factor (where material)
checks.description: Risk factors should address material climate / environmental / ESG risks where applicable.

checks.name: Update vs prior periodic report (10-K only)
checks.description: 10-K risk factors should update / cross-reference prior-period risk factors (S-K Item 105 + Form 10-K Instructions).

checks.name: Prose only — financial statements and filing schemas are not checked
checks.description: States on every regulatory-filing analysis that Vaulytica checks only the drafter's prose — not financial statements, numbers, or filing schemas.

checks.name: Declarant identification + capacity recital

checks.name: Pain management / comfort care directive

checks.name: Organ donation / anatomical gift

checks.name: Witness requirements + notarial acknowledgment
checks.description: Advance directive must include execution block with witnesses (and notarization where required).

checks.name: Effective-date / triggering condition
checks.description: Advance directive must state when it becomes effective (incapacity / terminal condition).

checks.name: Revocation method
checks.description: Advance directive should describe how it may be revoked (writing / oral statement / destruction).

checks.name: Execution formalities cannot be verified from text alone

types.name: AI Usage Addendum
types.summary: Linter for an AI / Generative-AI Addendum to a commercial agreement. Checks cover definitions (Generative AI / Foundation Model / Output / Training Data), prohibited training-on-customer-data without opt-in, transparency (features + default state + hosting), IP ownership of outputs, AI hallucination disclaimer + human-review obligation, AI subprocessor disclosure, deletion of fine-tuning data on termination. Citations are NIST AI RMF / EU AI Act / FTC enforcement — explicitly labeled 'consensus practice, not statute' where no controlling regulator applies.

checks.name: AI definitions present
checks.description: AI Addendum must define the core terms (Generative AI, Foundation Model, Output, Training Data).

checks.name: Prohibited use: training on customer data without opt-in
checks.description: Flags an AI Addendum that permits training on customer data without an explicit opt-in.

checks.name: AI transparency: features + default state + hosting
checks.description: AI Addendum should disclose which features use AI, whether on by default or opt-in, and whether the model is on-prem or third-party-hosted.

checks.name: IP ownership of AI outputs
checks.description: AI Addendum must allocate IP ownership of Outputs.

checks.name: AI output warranty disclaimer + human-review obligation
checks.description: AI Addendum should disclaim warranties on AI outputs (hallucination risk) and obligate human review for high-stakes uses.

checks.name: AI subprocessor disclosure
checks.description: AI Addendum should disclose AI subprocessors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.).

checks.name: Deletion of fine-tuning data on termination
checks.description: AI Addendum should obligate deletion of fine-tuning / training data on termination.

types.name: AI Acceptable Use Policy

checks.name: Approved AI tools list + procurement gate

checks.name: Prohibited inputs — PHI / PII / trade-secret / privileged

checks.name: Human-in-the-loop review for high-impact outputs

checks.name: IP / attribution / hallucination disclaimer

types.name: Business Associate Agreement (HIPAA)
types.summary: Covered-entity to business-associate BAA under HIPAA. Checks cover 45 CFR § 164.504(e) required clauses, § 164.314(a) Security Rule flow-down, § 164.410 breach notification, plus HHS-guidance posture rules.

checks.name: Permitted uses and disclosures of PHI
checks.description: BAA must establish the permitted and required uses and disclosures of PHI by the business associate.

checks.name: Use limited to permitted purposes
checks.description: Business associate may not use PHI for any purpose other than as permitted by the BAA or required by law.

checks.name: Appropriate safeguards clause
checks.description: BAA must require BA to use appropriate safeguards, including Security Rule administrative, physical, and technical safeguards.

checks.name: Report improper uses or disclosures
checks.description: BAA must require BA to report to the covered entity any use or disclosure not provided for by the contract.

checks.name: Subcontractor flow-down
checks.description: BA must ensure subcontractors that handle PHI agree in writing to the same restrictions and conditions.

checks.name: Access to PHI (164.524)
checks.description: BAA must require BA to make PHI available in a Designated Record Set to satisfy 45 CFR 164.524.

checks.name: Amendment of PHI (164.526)
checks.description: BAA must require BA to make PHI available for amendment to satisfy 45 CFR 164.526.

checks.name: Accounting of disclosures (164.528)
checks.description: BAA must require BA to maintain and make available the information required to provide an accounting of disclosures.

checks.name: Books and records available to HHS Secretary
checks.description: BAA must require BA to make its internal practices, books, and records available to HHS for compliance review.

checks.name: Return or destruction at termination
checks.description: BA must, at termination, return or destroy all PHI received from, or created on behalf of, the covered entity.

checks.name: Termination right for material breach
checks.description: Covered entity must have the right to terminate the BAA for material breach by the business associate.

checks.name: Authorization to terminate if cure infeasible
checks.description: BAA should authorize termination when cure of a material breach is not feasible.

checks.name: Security Rule compliance required
checks.description: BAA must require BA to comply, where applicable, with the Security Rule with respect to ePHI.

checks.name: Administrative safeguards referenced
checks.description: BAA should reference administrative safeguards required by the Security Rule.

checks.name: Physical safeguards referenced
checks.description: BAA should reference physical safeguards required by the Security Rule.

checks.name: Technical safeguards referenced
checks.description: BAA should reference technical safeguards required by the Security Rule.

checks.name: Security incident reporting
checks.description: BAA must require BA to report security incidents to the covered entity.

checks.name: Subcontractor flow-down for Security Rule
checks.description: BA must ensure subcontractors handling ePHI agree to the Security Rule restrictions.

checks.name: Breach notification clause present
checks.description: BAA must require BA to notify the covered entity of a breach of unsecured PHI.

checks.name: Breach notification looser than 60 days
checks.description: Flags breach-notice timing that exceeds the 60-day outer bound or shifts the trigger to a later event.

checks.name: Breach trigger is 'discovery'
checks.description: Breach-notification timing should be measured from 'discovery,' not a stricter post-discovery event.

checks.name: 'Without unreasonable delay' language present
checks.description: BAA should include 'without unreasonable delay' to match HIPAA's inner timing bound.

checks.name: Security Incident narrowed to 'successful' access
checks.description: Flags clauses that limit 'Security Incident' to only successful unauthorized accesses — a narrowing OCR has criticized.

checks.name: Return-or-destruction lacks definite outer bound
checks.description: Flags return-or-destruction language that is open-ended ('as soon as practicable', 'commercially reasonable').

checks.name: Indemnity cap impairing HIPAA remedies
checks.description: Flags liability caps that limit damages below the covered entity's potential HIPAA penalty exposure.

checks.name: Covered entity audit rights preserved
checks.description: BAA should preserve the covered entity's right to audit BA's HIPAA compliance.

checks.name: Covered entity indemnifies BA for HIPAA violations
checks.description: Flags clauses where the covered entity indemnifies the business associate for HIPAA violations — a common vendor overreach.

checks.name: PHI / ePHI defined or cross-referenced
checks.description: BAA should define PHI/ePHI or cross-reference the HIPAA definition.

checks.name: Minimum-necessary standard referenced
checks.description: BAA should reference HIPAA's minimum-necessary standard.

checks.name: Mitigation obligation
checks.description: BAA should require BA to mitigate harmful effects of any improper use or disclosure.

checks.name: Workforce training requirement
checks.description: BAA should require BA's workforce members handling PHI to be trained on its obligations.

checks.name: Encryption or NIST safeguards referenced
checks.description: BAA should reference encryption / NIST-style safeguards for ePHI at rest and in transit.

checks.name: Risk assessment requirement
checks.description: BAA should require BA to conduct periodic risk assessments per § 164.308(a)(1).

checks.name: Sanctions policy / personnel discipline
checks.description: BAA should reference BA's sanctions policy for workforce members who violate HIPAA/BAA.

checks.name: Subprocessor / vendor disclosure
checks.description: BAA should require BA to disclose subprocessors / downstream vendors that handle PHI.

checks.name: Signed by authorized representative
checks.description: BAA should be signed by an authorized representative of each party (satisfactory assurances).

checks.name: Effective date present
checks.description: BAA should state an effective date.

checks.name: Term / duration clause present
checks.description: BAA should specify its term.

checks.name: Governing law specified
checks.description: BAA should specify the governing law.

checks.name: Notice clause present
checks.description: BAA should specify how formal notices (including breach notices) are delivered.

checks.name: PHI referenced in document
checks.description: BAA should explicitly reference PHI or ePHI; absence likely means the wrong template.

checks.name: Choice-of-law overrides federal HIPAA
checks.description: Flags clauses that purport to make state law control over HIPAA — preempted but indicates poor drafting.

checks.name: Survival of HIPAA obligations after termination
checks.description: BAA should state that HIPAA-related obligations survive termination.

checks.name: Definitions track current HIPAA terminology
checks.description: BAA should track current HIPAA / HITECH terminology (Breach, Unsecured PHI, Covered Entity, Business Associate).

checks.name: Covered entity / business associate roles named
checks.description: BAA should clearly identify which party is the Covered Entity and which is the Business Associate.

types.summary: Bylaws of a Delaware (or MBCA-modeled) corporation.

checks.description: Bylaws must state who may adopt and amend them (board, stockholders, or both) per DGCL § 109 / MBCA § 10.20.

checks.description: Bylaws must designate the time / place / mode of the annual meeting of stockholders (DGCL § 211; MBCA § 7.01).

checks.name: Special meeting call right specified
checks.description: Bylaws should state who may call a special meeting of stockholders (DGCL § 211(d); MBCA § 7.02).

checks.name: Notice of meetings provisions
checks.description: Bylaws must set notice timing for stockholder meetings (DGCL § 222; MBCA § 7.05).

checks.name: Quorum for stockholder meetings
checks.description: Bylaws must state the quorum required for stockholder meetings (DGCL § 216; MBCA § 7.25).

checks.name: Directors — number, election, term
checks.description: Bylaws must specify the number of directors, election procedure, and term (DGCL § 141; MBCA § 8.03).

checks.name: Directors — removal and vacancies

checks.name: Indemnification of directors and officers

checks.name: Officers — designation

checks.name: Stock certificates / uncertificated shares

checks.name: Books and records inspection right

checks.description: CC&Rs should specify amendment procedure (typically supermajority of owners).

checks.name: Term / duration of restrictions
checks.description: CC&Rs should specify term (perpetual or set years) and automatic-extension mechanic.

checks.name: Race / discriminatory covenant flagged
checks.description: Discriminatory covenants based on race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, or disability are unenforceable (Shelley v. Kraemer; FHA 42 U.S.C. § 3604).

checks.name: Dispute resolution / enforcement
checks.description: CC&Rs should specify dispute resolution / enforcement procedure.

types.name: Cease-and-Desist Letter
types.summary: Cease-and-desist letter (IP, unfair competition, defamation). Lanham Act § 43(a) baseline; anti-SLAPP / extortion risk screen.

checks.name: Identification of protected IP / right
checks.description: Cease-and-desist must identify the specific IP, mark, copyrighted work, or right alleged to be infringed.

checks.name: Description of allegedly infringing conduct
checks.description: C&D must describe the allegedly infringing conduct with specificity.

checks.name: Demand to cease and specific remedial actions
checks.description: C&D must demand cessation and specify the remedial actions (recall, transfer, accounting).

checks.name: Response deadline
checks.description: C&D must state a response deadline.

checks.name: Anti-SLAPP / extortion risk — overreaching threats flagged
checks.description: C&D should avoid threats of unrelated criminal prosecution or other overreach that may give rise to abuse-of-process / extortion / anti-SLAPP exposure.

types.name: Change Order
types.summary: Construction change order under AIA G701 baseline with contract-sum + time-adjustment summary.

checks.name: Original contract sum + revised contract sum
checks.description: Change order must reference the original contract sum and state the revised contract sum.

checks.name: Description of change in work
checks.description: Change order must describe the change in work (added, deleted, or modified items).

checks.name: Time impact — contract time adjustment
checks.description: Change order must address contract-time adjustment (or expressly state none).

checks.name: Signatures — owner + architect + contractor
checks.description: Change order must be signed by owner, architect, and contractor.

checks.name: Waiver of further claims for the changed work
checks.description: Change order should include a waiver of further claims related to the changed work.

types.name: Channel Partner / Referral Agreement
types.summary: Referral or channel-partner arrangement paying a fee for introduced business.

checks.name: Qualified-referral / lead definition
checks.description: A referral agreement must define what counts as a qualified referral or lead that earns a fee.

checks.name: Referral-fee amount and payment terms
checks.description: A referral agreement should state the fee amount / rate and when and how it is paid.

checks.name: RESPA § 8 compliance for settlement-service referrals
checks.description: A referral fee tied to real-estate settlement services must comply with the RESPA § 8 anti-kickback prohibition.

checks.name: Independent contractor — no authority to bind
checks.description: A referral / channel partner must be an independent contractor with no authority to bind the principal.

checks.name: Anti-kickback / anti-bribery representation
checks.description: A referral arrangement should carry an anti-bribery / no-improper-payments representation.

checks.name: Confidentiality of leads and customer information
checks.description: A referral agreement should protect the confidentiality of referred leads and each party's customer information.

checks.name: Non-circumvention
checks.description: A referral agreement should bar the Partner from circumventing the Company to deal directly with a referred customer.

checks.name: Effect of termination on accrued and pipeline referral fees
checks.description: A referral agreement should state whether fees remain payable on referrals introduced before termination that close afterward (the 'tail').

checks.name: Restriction on Partner representations about the Company
checks.description: A referral agreement should bar the Partner from making representations about the Company or its products beyond Company-approved materials.

checks.name: Telemarketing / anti-spam compliance for Partner outreach
checks.description: Where the Partner solicits referrals by call, text, or email, the agreement should require TCPA / CAN-SPAM compliance.

types.name: Certificate / Articles of Incorporation
types.summary: Charter of a Delaware (or MBCA-modeled) corporation.

checks.name: Corporate name complies with statutory naming
checks.description: Charter must state the corporate name; DGCL § 102(a)(1) and MBCA § 4.01 require a recognized corporate suffix.

checks.name: Registered office and registered agent
checks.description: Charter must designate registered office and agent (DGCL § 102(a)(2)).

checks.name: Purpose clause
checks.description: Charter must state the corporate purpose (DGCL § 102(a)(3); MBCA § 3.01).

checks.name: Authorized capital stock
checks.description: Charter must state the authorized capital stock — classes, shares, par value (DGCL § 102(a)(4); MBCA § 6.01).

checks.name: Incorporator name and address
checks.description: Charter must identify the incorporator (DGCL § 102(a)(5); MBCA § 2.01).

checks.name: Director-exculpation clause (DGCL § 102(b)(7))
checks.description: Charter should include the optional § 102(b)(7) director-exculpation clause; absent it, directors are exposed to monetary liability for breaches of fiduciary duty of care.

checks.name: Indemnification authorization in charter
checks.description: Charter should authorize indemnification under DGCL § 145; bylaws then implement.

checks.name: Stockholder action by written consent (DGCL § 228) addressed
checks.description: Charter should address whether stockholders may act by written consent (DGCL § 228).

checks.name: Preferred-stock blank check authority
checks.description: Charter should grant the board blank-check preferred-stock authority (DGCL § 151(g)).

checks.name: Amendment of certificate of incorporation
checks.description: Charter should address amendment procedures (DGCL § 242).

No conditioning participation on excess collection

Data ownership, access, and records retention

checks.name: Compliance with laws + regulations

checks.name: NLRA § 7 — overbroad social-media restriction flagged
checks.description: Social-media policy must not broadly restrict employee discussion of wages / working conditions (NLRA § 7).

types.name: Conflict of Interest Policy
types.summary: Conflict of interest policy under IRS Form 990 + IRC § 4958 + state nonprofit law.

checks.name: Definition of conflict of interest
checks.description: Policy must define what constitutes a conflict of interest.

checks.name: Annual disclosure / certification + ongoing duty
checks.description: Policy must require annual disclosure + ongoing duty to disclose new conflicts.

checks.name: Sanctions for violations

checks.description: Audit committee must have authority to engage and pay independent counsel / advisors.

checks.name: Meetings — frequency and minimum

checks.name: Reporting to the full board
checks.description: Committee charter must require periodic reporting to the full board.

checks.name: Charter review and amendment
checks.description: Committee charter must be reviewed and reassessed annually.

checks.name: Audit committee — non-independent member prohibited
checks.description: Charter cannot allow a non-independent member to serve on the audit committee absent the § 301 controlled-company / phase-in exception.

Jury demand where a jury is wanted

types.name: Confidential Settlement Agreement
types.summary: Confidential settlement agreement with NLRB *McLaren Macomb*, SEC Rule 21F-17 carve-out, and IRC § 162(q) compliance.

checks.name: California § 1542 waiver (if applicable)

checks.name: Whistleblower / agency-communication carve-out
checks.description: Confidential settlements must preserve the parties' right to communicate with regulators (SEC Rule 21F-17, EEOC, NLRB, DOL).

checks.name: Tax allocation / IRS Form 1099 / W-2 treatment
checks.description: Settlement of employment / personal-injury / contract claims should allocate payment among taxable categories.

checks.name: Section 162(q) — Harvey Weinstein tax limitation (sexual harassment claims)
checks.description: IRC § 162(q) disallows deduction of settlements subject to nondisclosure for sexual harassment / abuse.

checks.name: Amount, payment terms, and default acceleration

types.name: Construction Contract (AIA-style)
types.summary: AIA A101 / A201-style owner-contractor agreement with anti-indemnity screen.

checks.name: Owner / contractor / architect identified
checks.description: Construction contract must identify owner, contractor, and (if applicable) architect.

checks.name: Scope of work / contract documents
checks.description: Contract must define the scope of work and incorporate the contract documents (drawings, specs, addenda).

checks.name: Contract sum + price / payment terms
checks.description: Contract must state contract sum (stipulated sum / GMP / cost-plus) and progress payments.

checks.name: Time of completion + liquidated damages
checks.description: Contract must establish time of completion (commencement + substantial completion + final completion) and liquidated-damages if applicable.

checks.name: Differing site conditions clause
checks.description: Contract should address differing site conditions (Type I — concealed conditions; Type II — unknown conditions).

checks.name: Indemnification + insurance + waiver of subrogation
checks.description: Contract must include indemnification, insurance requirements, and waiver-of-subrogation provisions consistent with state anti-indemnity statutes.

checks.name: Termination — convenience + cause
checks.description: Contract must include termination for cause AND termination for convenience.

types.name: Construction Lien Waiver

checks.name: Waiver type — conditional / unconditional + progress / final
checks.description: Lien waiver must identify type: conditional vs unconditional, progress vs final.

checks.name: Identified claimant + property + project
checks.description: Lien waiver must identify the claimant, the property / project, and the through-date / payment amount.

checks.name: Scope of waiver — limited to amount received / through-date
checks.description: Waiver must limit its effect to the amount actually received and through the stated date.

checks.name: Conditional waiver — payment condition
checks.description: Conditional waivers must condition effectiveness on actual receipt of payment.

checks.name: Carve-outs — disputed claims / future rights
checks.description: Waiver should preserve carve-outs for retention, disputed claims, items not within waiver, and future rights.

checks.name: Signature + date + statutory form recital
checks.description: Lien waiver must be signed and dated; in states using prescribed forms, the form recital must appear verbatim.

types.name: Consulting Agreement

types.name: Contingency Fee Agreement
types.summary: Contingent fee agreement measured against ABA Model Rule 1.5(c).

checks.name: Signed writing stating the contingency method
Expenses deducted before or after the fee
Expenses owed if there is no recovery
Matters excluded from the contingent fee
Statement of the outcome at conclusion

types.name: Contributor License Agreement (CLA)
types.summary: OSS contributor license agreement (ASF ICLA / corporate CCLA pattern) with defensive-termination patent grant.

checks.name: Contributor identification + entity / individual disambiguation
checks.description: CLA must identify the contributor and disambiguate individual vs entity contribution.

checks.name: Copyright license grant to project
checks.description: CLA must grant a copyright license sufficient for the project to use, modify, and redistribute.

checks.name: Patent license grant + defensive termination
checks.description: CLA must grant a patent license and include defensive termination.

checks.name: Original-work representation
checks.description: Contributor must represent that the contribution is their original work or properly licensed.

checks.name: DCO alternative path (sign-off)
checks.description: Projects following the DCO model should accept signed-off-by per the Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1.

types.name: Convertible Promissory Note
types.summary: Convertible promissory note (UCC Article 3 negotiable instrument convertible into preferred stock at next qualified financing).

checks.name: Principal amount stated
checks.description: Convertible note must state principal (UCC § 3-104 — unconditional promise to pay a fixed amount).

checks.name: Interest rate stated
checks.description: Convertible note should state interest rate (vs. SAFE which does not bear interest).

checks.name: Interest rate above plausible usury threshold
checks.description: Most state usury caps for non-bank lenders sit in the 7–24% range; rates above 25% are heuristically usurious in many states.

checks.name: Maturity date specified
checks.description: Convertible note must have a maturity date.

checks.name: Qualified financing / conversion mechanics
checks.description: Convertible note must define qualified-financing trigger and conversion price (discount and/or cap).

checks.name: Change-of-control treatment
checks.description: Convertible note must address change of control before conversion.

checks.name: Subordination acknowledgment
checks.description: Convertible notes are typically subordinate to senior debt — clause should say so.

checks.name: Events of default enumerated
checks.description: Convertible note must enumerate events of default.

checks.name: Investor accredited-investor representation
checks.description: Convertible notes are sold under Reg D Rule 506; investor must represent accredited-investor status.

types.name: Cookie / Tracking Notice
types.summary: Cookie / tracking notice with ePrivacy + GDPR Art. 7 consent and CCPA / CPRA opt-out (GPC).

checks.name: Cookie categories disclosed (strictly necessary / functional / analytics / advertising)
checks.description: Cookie notice must categorize cookies (strictly necessary, functional / preferences, analytics / performance, targeting / advertising).

checks.name: Consent mechanism (opt-in for non-essential)
checks.description: Cookie notice must disclose the consent mechanism for non-essential cookies (banner / preference center).

checks.name: Per-cookie disclosure — name / provider / purpose / duration
checks.description: Cookie notice should disclose per-cookie details: name, provider, purpose, and retention duration.

checks.name: Withdraw consent — instructions
checks.description: Cookie notice must explain how users can withdraw consent (as easy as giving it — GDPR Art. 7(3)).

checks.name: CCPA / CPRA opt-out (Sale / Share / Cross-context targeted advertising)
checks.description: Cookie notice for CCPA / CPRA-covered businesses must explain the right to opt out of sale / share / cross-context targeted advertising (GPC support).

checks.name: Third-party recipients / international transfers
checks.description: Cookie notice must disclose third-party recipients and any international transfers.

types.name: Copyright License Agreement
types.summary: Copyright license with 17 U.S.C. § 204 writing requirement and § 106 rights enumeration.

checks.name: Licensed Works identified
checks.description: Copyright license must identify Licensed Works (titles, registration numbers, deposit info).

checks.name: Exclusive vs non-exclusive + signed writing for exclusive grants
checks.description: Copyright license must state exclusivity; exclusive grants must satisfy 17 U.S.C. § 204(a) (signed writing).

checks.name: Rights granted — reproduction / distribution / display / performance / derivative
checks.description: Copyright license must specify which 17 U.S.C. § 106 rights are granted.

checks.name: Term, territory, media / channels
checks.description: Copyright license must specify term, territory, and media / channels of use.

checks.name: Attribution / credit / moral rights
checks.description: Copyright license should address attribution and moral-rights treatment.

checks.name: Termination of transfers — 17 U.S.C. § 203 caveat
checks.description: Copyright license should acknowledge the § 203 termination-of-transfers right (35–40 year window).

checks.description: Deed of trust must identify grantor (trustor), trustee, and beneficiary (mortgagor / mortgagee for mortgage states).

checks.name: Legal description of real property

checks.description: Mortgage / deed of trust must contain a granting clause conveying the property to trustee / mortgagee.

checks.name: Power of sale / judicial foreclosure election

checks.name: Due-on-sale + due-on-encumbrance
checks.description: Mortgage / deed of trust should include due-on-sale and due-on-encumbrance acceleration triggers.

checks.name: Recording acknowledgment + governing-law / homestead waiver
checks.description: Instrument should include a notarial acknowledgment and address homestead / dower / spousal-consent where applicable.

types.name: Demand Letter

types.name: DPA — Controller to Processor (EU/UK)
types.summary: Data Processing Agreement under GDPR and UK GDPR. Checks cover Article 28(3) enumerated clauses, Articles 28(2)/(4)/(9) subprocessor governance, Articles 27, 30, 32, 33(2), 35, 37, and Chapter V international transfers.

checks.name: Subject-matter of processing identified
checks.description: DPA must identify the subject-matter of the processing.

checks.name: Duration of processing specified
checks.description: DPA must specify the duration of the processing.

checks.name: Nature and purpose of processing
checks.description: DPA must describe the nature and purpose of the processing.

checks.name: Type of personal data identified
checks.description: DPA must identify the type of personal data processed.

checks.name: Categories of data subjects identified
checks.description: DPA must identify the categories of data subjects.

checks.name: Obligations and rights of the controller stated
checks.description: DPA must state the obligations and rights of the controller.

checks.name: Processing only on documented instructions
checks.description: Processor must process personal data only on documented instructions from the controller.

checks.name: Confidentiality of authorised persons
checks.description: Persons authorised to process personal data must commit themselves to confidentiality.

checks.name: Article 32 security measures incorporated
checks.description: DPA must require the processor to take all measures required pursuant to Article 32.

checks.name: Subprocessor terms (Art. 28(2) and (4))
checks.description: DPA must respect the conditions for engaging another processor.

checks.name: Assist controller in responding to data-subject rights
checks.description: Processor must assist the controller in responding to data-subject rights requests.

checks.name: Assist controller with Articles 32–36 obligations
checks.description: Processor must assist the controller with Articles 32–36 obligations (security, breach, DPIA, prior consultation).

checks.name: Deletion or return at end of services
checks.description: Processor must, at the choice of the controller, delete or return all personal data after the end of the provision of services.

checks.name: Information available for compliance demonstration
checks.description: Processor must make available all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with Article 28.

checks.name: Subprocessor prior written authorisation (Art. 28(2))
checks.description: Processor must obtain prior specific or general written authorisation before engaging a subprocessor.

checks.name: Subprocessor change notification + objection right
checks.description: Where general authorisation is used, controller must be informed of intended changes and have the opportunity to object.

checks.name: Subprocessor flow-down of same obligations (Art. 28(4))
checks.description: Where the processor engages a subprocessor, the same data-protection obligations must be imposed on the subprocessor by contract.

checks.name: DPA in writing including electronic form
checks.description: DPA must be in writing, including in electronic form.

checks.name: Pseudonymisation / encryption referenced
checks.description: Art. 32(1)(a) lists pseudonymisation and encryption as appropriate measures where relevant.

checks.name: Confidentiality / integrity / availability / resilience
checks.description: Art. 32(1)(b) — ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems.

checks.name: Restore availability after incident
checks.description: Art. 32(1)(c) — ability to restore availability and access to personal data in a timely manner.

checks.name: Regular testing of measures
checks.description: Art. 32(1)(d) — process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating effectiveness.

checks.name: 'Appropriate measures' undefined hand-waving
checks.description: Flags DPAs that reference 'appropriate measures' without an Annex of technical and organisational measures.

checks.name: Processor breach notice to controller (Art. 33(2))
checks.description: Processor must notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.

checks.name: 'Without undue delay' present
checks.description: Breach-notification clause should include 'without undue delay'.

checks.name: Breach-notice content elements (Art. 33(3))
checks.description: Breach notification should include the Article 33(3) content elements (nature, categories, contact, consequences, measures).

checks.name: Breach notice timing stricter than 'undue delay'
checks.description: Flags fixed breach-notice deadlines that exceed regulator expectations (e.g., > 72 hours from controller awareness, > 5 days from processor awareness).

checks.name: Article 30 records of processing assistance
checks.description: Processor should assist controller with Art. 30 records of processing activities (RoPA).

checks.name: DPIA assistance (Art. 35)
checks.description: Processor should assist controller with Data Protection Impact Assessments under Art. 35.

checks.name: Article 27 EU representative referenced (where applicable)
checks.description: Non-EU processors should reference their EU representative under Art. 27.

checks.name: Article 37 DPO referenced (where applicable)
checks.description: Where required, the DPA should reference the Data Protection Officer under Art. 37.

checks.name: International transfer mechanism named
checks.description: Where international transfers occur, the DPA must name a Chapter V mechanism.

checks.name: EU SCCs incorporated by reference
checks.description: DPA should incorporate EU SCCs by reference where transfers require them.

checks.name: Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) referenced
checks.description: Following Schrems II, parties should reference a TIA where Chapter V transfers occur.

checks.name: Deletion-or-return choice belongs to processor
checks.description: Flags clauses where the processor (not the controller) chooses between deletion and return.

checks.name: Audit-substitution eliminates audit entirely
checks.description: Flags SOC 2 / ISO substitution that eliminates the controller's audit right rather than substituting it.

checks.name: Processor unilaterally amends instructions
checks.description: Flags clauses where the processor may deviate from controller instructions unilaterally.

checks.name: Personal data scope defined or annexed
checks.description: DPA should define personal data scope in an Annex (Annex I for SCCs).

checks.name: Technical and organisational measures annex
checks.description: DPA should include an Annex describing technical and organisational measures (Annex II for SCCs).

checks.name: Subprocessor list annex
checks.description: DPA should include a list of approved subprocessors (Annex III for SCCs Modules 2 & 3).

checks.name: GDPR-current terminology (Personal Data Breach defined)
checks.description: DPA should track GDPR terminology (Personal Data Breach, Data Subject, Processor, Controller).

checks.name: Controller / Processor roles named
checks.description: DPA should clearly identify which party is the Controller and which is the Processor.

checks.name: Signature block present
checks.description: DPA should be signed by an authorised representative of each party.

checks.name: Effective date present
checks.description: DPA should state an effective date.

checks.name: Term and termination clauses
checks.description: DPA should state its term and termination conditions.

checks.name: Governing-law clause present
checks.description: DPA should specify governing law (typically EU Member State or UK).

checks.name: Liability allocation
checks.description: DPA should allocate liability between Controller and Processor.

checks.name: Controller indemnifies Processor for GDPR fines
checks.description: Flags clauses where the controller indemnifies the processor for the processor's own GDPR liability.

checks.name: Processor caps audit cost on controller exclusively
checks.description: Flags clauses where the controller must bear the entire cost of any audit, including audits triggered by processor breach.

checks.name: Personal data referenced in document
checks.description: DPA should reference 'personal data'; absence likely means the wrong template.

checks.name: Notice clause present
checks.description: DPA should specify how formal notices (including breach notices) are delivered.

checks.name: Survival of GDPR obligations post-termination
checks.description: DPA should state that obligations applicable to retained personal data survive termination.

checks.name: Records of subprocessor changes available
checks.description: Processor should keep records of subprocessor changes available on request.

checks.name: Onward transfer obligations (SCC Clause 8.8)
checks.description: Where SCCs apply, the DPA should reference onward-transfer obligations per SCC Clause 8.8.

checks.name: Local-law disclosure obligations (Clause 14 / 15)
checks.description: Where SCCs apply, processor must notify controller of legally-binding requests by public authorities.

checks.name: Adequacy: reliance on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework
checks.description: Flags reliance on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (or its UK extension) so the importer's certification and a fallback transfer mechanism are confirmed.

checks.name: Adequacy decision currency clause
checks.description: Where an adequacy decision is relied on, the DPA should anchor the reliance with a fallback for invalidation.

checks.name: TIA / Transfer Risk Assessment reference
checks.description: Where SCCs / IDTA cover transfers to a non-adequate country, the DPA must reference a TIA / TRA.

checks.name: Onward-transfer terms (Clause 8.7 / 8.8)
checks.description: Where SCCs apply, the DPA should address onward-transfer terms per SCC Clause 8.7 / 8.8.

types.name: Data Protection Impact Assessment (GDPR Art. 35)
types.summary: GDPR Art. 35 DPIA covering necessity, proportionality, risk assessment, and mitigations.

checks.name: Systematic description of processing — Art. 35(7)(a)
checks.description: DPIA must contain a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and purposes.

checks.name: Necessity and proportionality assessment — Art. 35(7)(b)
checks.description: DPIA must assess the necessity and proportionality of processing in relation to the purposes.

checks.name: Risk assessment — likelihood and severity
checks.description: DPIA must assess the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects (likelihood × severity).

checks.name: Mitigation measures and safeguards
checks.description: DPIA must describe the measures envisaged to address the risks (technical, organisational, contractual).

checks.name: DPO consultation
checks.description: DPIA must record the DPO's advice (Art. 35(2)) and the controller's decision (whether followed).

checks.name: Prior consultation trigger (Art. 36)
checks.description: If residual high risk remains, DPIA must record the Art. 36 prior-consultation analysis.

types.name: Durable Power of Attorney (Financial)
types.summary: Durable POA under UPOAA + state POA statutes with 'hot powers' specific grant. Execution formalities cannot be verified from text alone.

checks.name: Principal + agent identification (financial)
checks.description: Durable POA must identify principal and agent (and successor agent).

checks.name: Durable language — survives incapacity
checks.description: POA must include durable language stating it survives principal's incapacity.

checks.name: Scope of agent's authority — categories / hot powers
checks.description: POA must enumerate scope (real property, banks, taxes, business, gifts, etc.); 'hot powers' (gifts, beneficiary changes) require specific authority.

checks.name: Springing vs immediate effectiveness
checks.description: POA must state whether it is immediately effective or springing (on incapacity).

checks.name: Agent's duties — fiduciary obligations
checks.description: POA should recite agent's fiduciary duties (UPOAA § 114): loyalty, good faith, no commingling.

checks.name: Third-party reliance / acceptance protection
checks.description: POA should provide third-party reliance / acceptance protection (UPOAA § 119 / § 120).

checks.name: Notarial acknowledgment + recording (for real property)
checks.description: Durable POA must be notarized; recording is needed where real property is involved.

checks.name: Execution formalities cannot be verified from text alone
checks.description: States on every trust, estate and family-law analysis that execution formalities (witnesses, notary, holographic and other state-specific requirements) cannot be verified from the document's text.

types.name: Earnout Agreement
types.summary: Post-closing contingent-consideration earnout (Delaware *Lazard / Aveta* line).

checks.name: Earnout period and milestones defined
checks.description: Earnout must define period and specific, measurable milestones.

checks.name: Definition of 'Revenue' / 'EBITDA' for earnout
checks.description: Earnouts based on revenue / EBITDA must define those metrics precisely.

checks.name: Conduct-of-business covenant during earnout period
checks.description: Buyer should covenant to operate the business in a way consistent with achieving earnout milestones.

checks.name: Implied covenant — express acknowledgment or waiver
checks.description: Delaware Lazard held that the implied covenant cannot be waived; the agreement should not purport to do so.

checks.name: Disclaimer of obligation to maximize earnout
checks.description: Disclaimers of any duty to maximize the earnout will not survive — Lazard still applies.

checks.name: Earnout calculation and payment mechanics
checks.description: Earnout must specify calculation, statement-delivery, dispute, and payment timing.

checks.name: Right of set-off against earnout
checks.description: Earnout often includes a right of set-off against indemnification obligations.

checks.name: Acceleration on change of control
checks.description: Earnout should address acceleration if buyer undergoes a subsequent change of control.

checks.name: Tax treatment of earnout (imputed interest)
checks.description: Earnouts can trigger imputed-interest treatment under IRC § 483 / § 1274.

types.name: Easement Agreement
types.summary: Real-property easement agreement (appurtenant / in gross; affirmative / negative).

checks.name: Servient and dominant tenement identified
checks.description: Easement agreement must identify servient (burdened) and dominant (benefited) parcels.

checks.name: Easement type stated (appurtenant vs in gross; affirmative vs negative)
checks.description: Easement agreement should state the type of easement.

checks.name: Scope of use
checks.description: Easement must define scope of use (purpose, intensity, vehicles, hours).

checks.name: Maintenance and repair allocation
checks.description: Easement should allocate maintenance and repair costs.

checks.name: Indemnification and insurance
checks.description: Easement should include indemnification and insurance covenant.

checks.name: Term / termination conditions
checks.description: Easement should state term (perpetual vs term) and termination triggers.

checks.name: Recording covenant
checks.description: Easement must be recorded to bind successors (state recording acts).

types.name: Employee Handbook
types.summary: Employee handbook (scoped subset — at-will, EEO, wage/hour, leave, social media, acknowledgment).

checks.name: At-will employment statement / no contract disclaimer
checks.description: Handbook must contain an at-will / no-contract disclaimer.

checks.name: EEO / anti-harassment policy
checks.description: Handbook must include an EEO / anti-harassment policy with complaint procedure.

checks.name: FLSA / wage and hour compliance section
checks.description: Handbook should address FLSA compliance — classification, overtime, timekeeping.

checks.name: Leave policies (FMLA + state)
checks.description: Handbook should cover FMLA + state-required leaves (CFRA, NYPFL, etc.).

checks.name: NLRA § 7 overbroad confidentiality / social-media policy
checks.description: Overbroad confidentiality / social-media / non-disparagement rules can chill protected concerted activity (NLRA § 7).

checks.name: Handbook acknowledgment receipt page
checks.description: Handbook must include an acknowledgment-of-receipt page.

types.name: Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
types.summary: § 423 employee stock purchase plan, reviewed against the qualification conditions in 26 U.S.C. § 423(b).

types.name: Employment Agreement, US, at-will, exempt
types.summary: Standard US offer-letter-style employment agreement for exempt, at-will employees. Based on GitHub's Balanced Employee IP Agreement and published Cooley offer-letter templates.

types.name: Employment Restrictive Covenant Agreement
types.summary: Employment-side non-compete / non-solicit covenant. Subject to FTC NCR § 910 and state non-compete law.

checks.name: Worker non-compete — state-law enforceability scrutiny
checks.description: Worker non-competes turn on state law; the FTC's 2024 rule that would have banned most of them (16 C.F.R. Part 910) was vacated and never took effect.

checks.name: Non-compete duration stated
checks.description: Where permitted, non-compete duration must be stated.

checks.name: Non-solicit of customers and employees
checks.description: Employment RC should include customer / employee non-solicits.

checks.name: Geographic scope tied to actual market
checks.description: Geographic scope should be reasonable and tied to where the employee worked.

checks.name: Consideration for restrictive covenants
checks.description: Restrictive covenants must be supported by consideration; some states require independent consideration mid-employment (e.g., MA, IL).

checks.name: Garden-leave option (MA / WA where required)
checks.description: Massachusetts and Washington require garden leave or other consideration for post-employment non-competes.

checks.name: Blue-pencil / reformation clause
checks.description: Restrictive-covenant agreement should empower courts to reform overbroad terms.

types.name: HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices
types.summary: HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices under 45 C.F.R. § 164.520.

checks.name: Header statement — 45 C.F.R. § 164.520(b)(1)(i)
checks.description: NPP must include the prominent header statement: 'THIS NOTICE DESCRIBES HOW MEDICAL INFORMATION ABOUT YOU MAY BE USED AND DISCLOSED AND HOW YOU CAN GET ACCESS TO THIS INFORMATION. PLEASE REVIEW IT CAREFULLY.'

checks.name: Uses and disclosures — TPO + required + permitted + authorization
checks.description: NPP must describe uses and disclosures for treatment, payment, and health-care operations (TPO), plus required, permitted, and authorization-based disclosures.

checks.name: Individual rights enumeration — § 164.520(b)(1)(iv)
checks.description: NPP must enumerate individual rights: access, amendment, accounting, restriction, confidential communications, paper copy, breach notification.

checks.name: Covered entity duties statement
checks.description: NPP must describe the covered entity's duties (maintain privacy, provide notice, abide by current notice).

checks.name: Right to complain — HHS / OCR + no retaliation
checks.description: NPP must inform individuals of the right to complain to the covered entity and to HHS, and that the entity will not retaliate.

checks.name: Effective date of notice
checks.description: NPP must include an effective date.

checks.name: Contact information for privacy questions
checks.description: NPP must provide contact information for privacy questions.

checks.name: Specific high-sensitivity disclosure provisions (substance use / mental health / HIV / genetic)
checks.description: NPP should address specific protections that may apply to substance use, mental health, HIV, or genetic information.

types.name: Hold-Harmless Agreement
types.summary: Standalone hold-harmless agreement (typically participant / event release) with Tunkl-factor and assumption-of-risk screen.

checks.name: Parties identified
checks.description: Hold-harmless agreement must identify protected party and protecting party.

checks.name: Activity / scope of risk identified
checks.description: Hold-harmless agreement must identify the activity or scope of risk covered.

checks.name: Release-of-future-claims overreach flagged
checks.description: Pre-dispute hold-harmless agreements that release ordinary negligence may be unenforceable in some states (esp. for recreational / fitness activities for consumers).

checks.name: Acknowledgment of risk + assumption of risk language
checks.description: Hold-harmless should include an explicit acknowledgment of risk + assumption of risk where activity involves physical risk.

checks.name: Signature + date + minor / guardian recital (when applicable)
checks.description: Hold-harmless must be signed and dated; minor-participant forms need a guardian signature recital.

checks.name: Severability / partial-enforcement clause
checks.description: Hold-harmless should include severability so an over-broad portion does not void the whole.

types.name: Data-Incident Notification Template
types.summary: Data-incident / breach notification template covering GDPR Art. 33 / 34 + HIPAA + US state breach laws.

checks.name: Nature of the incident
checks.description: Incident notification must describe the nature of the personal-data breach.

checks.name: Categories and approximate number of data subjects / records affected
checks.description: Notification must identify categories and approximate numbers of data subjects and personal-data records affected.

checks.name: DPO / privacy contact information
checks.description: Notification must identify the DPO / privacy contact.

checks.name: Likely consequences for individuals
checks.description: Notification must describe the likely consequences of the breach.

checks.name: Measures taken / proposed to address the breach
checks.description: Notification must describe the measures taken / proposed to address the breach and mitigate consequences.

checks.name: Timing — 72 hour notification (GDPR Art. 33) + state thresholds
checks.description: Notification template must address GDPR Art. 33 72-hour timing and applicable state-specific thresholds.

checks.name: Regulatory / AG notification trigger threshold
checks.description: Template must address state-AG / supervisory-authority notification triggers (typically 500 / 1,000 affected residents).

types.name: Indemnification Agreement (standalone)
types.summary: Standalone indemnification agreement with anti-indemnity statute screen (NY § 5-322.1, CA § 2782, TX § 151).

checks.name: Indemnitor / indemnitee identified
checks.description: Indemnification agreement must identify indemnitor and indemnitee (and any third-party beneficiaries).

checks.name: Scope of indemnity — Type I / II / III recital
checks.description: Agreement should specify the indemnity type — limited form (Type III), intermediate form (Type II), or broad form (Type I) — with the operative language for the chosen form.

checks.name: Broad-form indemnity (Type I) flagged for anti-indemnity scrutiny
checks.description: Type I (broad-form) indemnity is void in construction contexts in many states (CA § 2782, NY § 5-322.1, TX § 151).

checks.name: Defense duty articulated separately from indemnity
checks.description: Agreement should separately articulate the duty to defend (broader than duty to indemnify under Crawford v. Weather Shield).

checks.name: Notice + tender + cooperation procedure
checks.description: Agreement must establish notice, tender, and cooperation procedure for indemnification claims.

checks.name: Insurance support — minimum limits matching indemnity
checks.description: Agreement should require insurance with limits matching the indemnity obligation (additional insured + waiver of subrogation).

checks.name: Survival of indemnity
checks.description: Agreement should state that indemnity obligations survive termination.

checks.name: Contact persons — research questions + research-related injury + subject rights

checks.name: FDA-regulated study — § 50.25 additional elements (when applicable)

checks.name: Compensation for injury (when applicable)

types.name: Insurance Endorsement Review

checks.description: Endorsement must identify its form number and edition date.

checks.name: Coverage being modified identified
