checks.description: Assignment must include assignor reps as to ownership and absence of encumbrances.

types.name: Irrevocable Trust
types.summary: Irrevocable trust instrument, reviewed for the irrevocability recital, spendthrift clause, trustee powers, and tax-sensitive terms.

types.name: Joint Development Agreement
types.summary: Collaborative R&D agreement, reviewed for background/foreground IP allocation, joint-inventorship default, and publication control.

checks.name: Foreground and joint IP ownership rule

types.name: Joint Representation Conflict Waiver
types.summary: Common-representation conflict waiver measured against ABA Model Rules 1.7 and 1.0(e).

checks.name: Identification of every jointly represented client
No confidentiality among the joint clients
Consequence if a conflict later develops
Advantages and risks of the common representation
Written confirmation signed by each client

types.name: Joint Venture Agreement
types.summary: Contractual or entity joint venture between US parties, covering governance, capital, deadlock, and exit.

checks.name: Scope and exclusivity of the venture
Transfer restrictions and exit or buy-sell

types.name: Last Will and Testament
types.summary: Last will and testament (text-only lint) under UPC §§ 2-501–509 + state will codes. Execution formalities cannot be verified from text alone.

checks.name: Testator identification + domicile
checks.description: Will must identify the testator and the testator's domicile.

checks.name: Revocation of prior wills + codicils
checks.description: Will must revoke prior wills and codicils.

checks.name: Executor / personal representative nomination
checks.description: Will must nominate an executor / personal representative (and successors).

checks.name: Bond waiver for fiduciaries
checks.description: Will should waive bond / surety for executor and other fiduciaries unless state law requires.

checks.name: Specific bequests + residuary clause
checks.description: Will must include a residuary clause (and identify any specific bequests).

checks.name: Guardianship nomination for minor children
checks.description: Wills involving minor children should nominate a guardian (and successors).

checks.name: Self-proving affidavit reference
checks.description: Will should reference a self-proving affidavit per UPC § 2-504 (most states recognize).

checks.name: Execution block — testator + witnesses (2)
checks.description: Will must include execution block for testator signature and at least two witnesses.

checks.name: Execution formalities cannot be verified from text alone
checks.description: States on every trust, estate and family-law analysis that execution formalities (witnesses, notary, holographic and other state-specific requirements) cannot be verified from the document's text.

types.name: Assignment of Lease
types.summary: Assignment of a commercial or residential lease with landlord consent and assignee assumption.

checks.name: Assignor / assignee / lease identification
checks.description: Assignment must identify assignor, assignee, and the underlying lease.

checks.name: Landlord consent
checks.description: Most commercial leases require landlord consent to assignment; the assignment should evidence that consent.

checks.name: Assumption of obligations by assignee
checks.description: Assignee should expressly assume all tenant obligations under the lease.

checks.name: Release of assignor (or continuing liability)
checks.description: Assignment should address whether assignor is released or remains liable.

checks.name: Effective date of assignment
checks.description: Assignment must state an effective date.

checks.name: Security deposit / prepaid rent transfer
checks.description: Assignment should address transfer of security deposit and any prepaid rent.

checks.name: Recording / notice to mortgagee
checks.description: Lease assignments may need to be recorded (memorandum of lease was recorded) and / or noticed to mortgagee under SNDA.

types.name: Commercial Real Estate Lease (Multi-Tenant Office, US)
types.summary: Multi-tenant US office lease with operating-expense pass-throughs. High-anxiety contract for small businesses. Drafting standards informed by the ABA Real Property section and Uniform Law Commission commentary.

types.name: Residential Lease (US)
types.summary: US residential lease. Pro se and consumer use case. Per-state variation is significant; treat governing law as the gating concern.

checks.name: Residential waiver of the warranty of habitability
checks.description: Detects a residential-lease term that waives the implied warranty of habitability or relieves the landlord of the duty to keep the premises habitable — void in nearly every state.

checks.name: Residential self-help eviction / lockout
checks.description: Detects a residential-lease term authorizing the landlord to lock out the tenant, shut off utilities, remove belongings, or retake possession without judicial process — self-help eviction, void in nearly every state.

checks.name: Residential security-deposit forfeiture / non-return
checks.description: Detects a residential-lease term declaring the security deposit non-refundable, forfeiting it on breach, or waiving the tenant's right to an itemized return — void in most states.

checks.name: Residential waiver of statutory tenant rights
checks.description: Detects a residential-lease term waiving the tenant's non-waivable statutory rights — all rights/remedies under the landlord-tenant act, the covenant of quiet enjoyment, or the right to notice — void in nearly every state.

types.name: Lease Letter of Intent
types.summary: Non-binding lease LOI, reviewed for the binding/non-binding split, exclusivity, and economic terms.

checks.name: Tenant improvement allowance and free rent
Expiration of the letter of intent

types.name: Limited Scope Representation Agreement
types.summary: Unbundled legal services agreement measured against ABA Model Rule 1.2(c).

checks.name: Tasks the lawyer will and will not perform
Reasonableness of the limitation for this matter
How and when the representation ends

types.name: Real Estate Listing Agreement
types.summary: Broker listing agreement, reviewed for the commission trigger, protection period, and agency-disclosure duties.

checks.name: Protection or tail period and registered buyers

types.name: Litigation Funding Agreement
types.summary: Third-party litigation funding agreement, reviewed for control, privilege/work-product, champerty, and disclosure-rule exposure.

checks.name: No funder control over litigation or settlement
Disclosure obligations under local rules and standing orders
Termination, budget overrun, and case-abandonment terms

types.name: Litigation Hold Notice
types.summary: Litigation hold / preservation notice (FRCP 37(e), *Zubulake*).

checks.name: Triggering event / pending or anticipated litigation
checks.description: Litigation hold must describe the triggering event (filed or anticipated litigation / investigation).

checks.name: Scope of preservation — categories of materials
checks.description: Hold notice must identify categories of materials to preserve (documents, emails, ESI, mobile, IM, voicemail).

checks.name: Suspension of routine deletion / retention policies
checks.description: Hold notice must suspend routine deletion / records-retention policies on covered materials.

checks.name: Custodian list and acknowledgment requirement
checks.description: Hold should identify covered custodians and require written acknowledgment.

checks.name: Point of contact for questions
checks.description: Hold notice should designate a point of contact (in-house or outside counsel) for questions.

checks.name: Privilege and confidentiality reminder
checks.description: Hold notice itself is typically privileged work-product; the notice should remind recipients not to share it externally.

types.name: Loan Agreement
types.summary: Commercial loan agreement (term / revolver) with affirmative + negative + financial covenants. LSTA / ABA model baseline.

checks.name: Default + acceleration
checks.description: Promissory note must address events of default and acceleration on default.

checks.name: Loan amount, facility type, purpose
checks.description: Loan agreement must state the loan amount, facility type (term / revolver), and use of proceeds.

checks.name: Interest rate / margin / floor
checks.description: Loan agreement must state the interest rate / margin / floor (SOFR / prime / fixed).

checks.name: Affirmative covenants
checks.description: Loan agreement must include affirmative covenants (financials, compliance, books-and-records).

checks.name: Negative covenants
checks.description: Loan agreement must include negative covenants (debt incurrence, liens, restricted payments, asset sales).

checks.name: Financial covenants
checks.description: Most loan agreements include financial covenants (leverage, interest coverage, fixed-charge coverage, minimum liquidity).

checks.name: Events of default + cross-default + cure periods
checks.description: Loan agreement must enumerate events of default with cure periods and cross-default to material indebtedness.

checks.name: Reg Z disclosures (consumer loans only)
checks.description: Consumer-purpose loans must include TILA / Reg Z disclosures (APR, finance charge, amount financed, total of payments).

checks.name: Confession of judgment / cognovit clause
checks.description: A confession-of-judgment (cognovit) clause lets the holder obtain judgment without notice or a hearing; it is void in consumer credit and prohibited or unenforceable in many states.

checks.name: Waiver of non-waivable Article 9 debtor protections
checks.description: Detects a security agreement or finance lease purporting to waive the debtor protections U.C.C. § 9-602 makes non-waivable — notice of disposition, commercial reasonableness, the right to redeem, the deficiency calculation, or the breach-of-the-peace limit on self-help repossession.

types.name: Lobbying / Political Contribution Policy
types.summary: Lobbying + political-contribution policy under federal LDA + FECA + state lobbying laws + federal gift rules.

checks.name: LDA registration + quarterly reporting
checks.description: Policy must address LDA registration thresholds + quarterly LD-2 reporting.

checks.name: Pre-approval of lobbying expenditures
checks.description: Policy must require pre-approval of lobbying expenditures and contacts with covered officials.

checks.name: Political contributions — corporate + individual + PAC
checks.description: Policy must address corporate political contributions (banned federally per FECA) + individual contributions + PAC procedures.

checks.name: State / local lobbying compliance
checks.description: Policy must address state / local lobbying registration and reporting (varies by jurisdiction).

checks.name: Gifts to government officials — strict prohibitions
checks.description: Policy must prohibit / strictly limit gifts to government officials (federal + state ethics codes).

types.name: Letter of Intent / Term Sheet
types.summary: Pre-definitive-agreement LOI or term sheet outlining commercial terms with binding / non-binding demarcation.

checks.name: Binding vs non-binding clause clearly demarcated
checks.description: LOIs must clearly demarcate binding (confidentiality, exclusivity, expenses, governing law) from non-binding (price, structure) provisions.

checks.name: Exclusivity / no-shop period stated
checks.description: LOI should include an exclusivity period during which the seller may not solicit competing offers.

checks.name: Confidentiality obligation
checks.description: Binding confidentiality clause is the universal binding LOI provision.

checks.name: Purchase price / consideration outline
checks.description: LOI should outline purchase price and consideration mix.

checks.name: Transaction structure outline
checks.description: LOI should outline the transaction structure (stock vs asset vs merger).

checks.name: Conditions to closing — outline
checks.description: LOI should outline conditions to closing (due diligence, financing, regulatory).

checks.name: Expenses / break fee treatment
checks.description: LOI should address whose expenses (party-pays vs reimbursement) and any break fee.

checks.name: Termination / expiration date
checks.description: LOI should have an expiration date (drop-dead date).

checks.name: Governing law / forum (binding)
checks.description: LOI should specify governing law and forum, declared binding.

types.name: Loyalty / Rewards Program Terms
types.summary: Consumer loyalty program terms, reviewed for points expiration, unilateral devaluation, and state gift-card overlaps.

checks.name: Account closure and transfer on death

types.name: M&A Restrictive Covenant Agreement
types.summary: Sale-of-business non-compete / non-solicit covenants, governed by state goodwill doctrine (e.g. Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16601). The FTC Non-Compete Clause Rule, whose § 910.2(a)(2) would likewise have preserved them, was set aside nationwide in Ryan LLC v. FTC and never took effect.

checks.name: Sale-of-business identification (goodwill nexus)
checks.description: Restrictive covenants must be tied to the sale of a business to qualify for the state-law sale-of-business exceptions (e.g., Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16601).

checks.name: Non-compete duration stated and bounded
checks.description: Non-compete duration should be stated and within enforceability norms (typically 2–5 years for M&A sales).

checks.name: Non-compete > 5 years flagged
checks.description: Most states will not enforce sale-of-business non-competes longer than 5 years.

checks.name: Geographic scope stated
checks.description: Non-compete must specify geographic scope.

checks.name: Activity scope (Competing Business defined)
checks.description: Non-compete must define what counts as Competing Business.

checks.name: Non-solicit of customers
checks.description: Non-solicit-of-customers covenant should be present.

checks.name: Non-solicit of employees
checks.description: Employee non-solicit (no-poach) should be present.

checks.name: Blue-pencil / reformation clause
checks.description: Restrictive-covenant agreement should empower courts to reform overbroad terms.

checks.name: Equitable relief and remedies
checks.description: Damages are usually inadequate; agreement should authorize injunctive relief without bond.

types.name: Manufacturing / Supply Agreement
types.summary: Supply of goods for manufacture or resale, governed by UCC Article 2.

checks.name: Quantity term — requirements / output / firm quantity
checks.description: A supply agreement must state a quantity term: a firm quantity, a requirements/output measure, or a binding forecast.

checks.name: Delivery schedule / lead time
checks.description: A supply agreement should state delivery timing — a schedule, lead time, or Incoterms delivery point.

checks.name: Specifications / conformance and warranty
checks.description: The goods must be tied to specifications and an express warranty of conformance.

checks.name: Price or price-adjustment mechanism
checks.description: A supply agreement should state the price or a mechanism for setting / adjusting it.

checks.name: Inspection, acceptance, and rejection
checks.description: Buyer should have a stated right to inspect, accept, and reject nonconforming goods.

checks.name: Force majeure / excuse for supervening events
checks.description: A supply agreement should allocate the risk of supervening events that prevent performance.

checks.name: Best-efforts obligation for a requirements / exclusive arrangement
checks.description: A requirements / output or exclusive-dealing supply arrangement must carry the § 2-306(2) best-efforts obligation.

checks.name: Warranty of title and against infringement
checks.description: Seller should warrant good title to the Goods, free of liens, and that the Goods do not infringe third-party rights.

checks.name: Limitation of remedies / exclusive remedy
checks.description: A supply agreement should state the buyer's exclusive remedy for nonconforming Goods (repair, replace, or refund).

checks.name: Implied warranty of merchantability / fitness — granted or disclaimed
checks.description: A supply agreement should address the UCC implied warranties — either affirm them or conspicuously disclaim them.

types.name: Marketing Services Agreement
types.summary: Engagement of a marketing agency to run campaigns / creative services. Part 255), CAN-SPAM compliance for email, ownership of deliverables, and advertising-claims substantiation (FTC Act § 5).

checks.name: Scope of services / deliverables / campaign
checks.description: A marketing services agreement must define the scope of services, deliverables, or the campaign.

checks.name: FTC endorsement / testimonial disclosure
checks.description: Marketing that uses endorsements, influencers, or testimonials must require the FTC-mandated material-connection disclosures.

checks.name: CAN-SPAM compliance for email marketing
checks.description: Email-marketing services must require CAN-SPAM compliance: accurate headers, an opt-out, and a physical address.

checks.name: Ownership of deliverables / work product
checks.description: A marketing services agreement should state who owns the creative deliverables and work product.

checks.name: Advertising-claims substantiation
checks.description: A marketing services agreement should require that advertising claims be truthful and substantiated.

checks.name: Consumer-data privacy compliance
checks.description: A marketing agreement under which the Agency handles consumer data should require privacy-law compliance and a data-processing term.

checks.name: Client approval rights over creative and claims
checks.description: A marketing agreement should reserve the Client's right to review and approve creative and public claims before release.

checks.name: Third-party rights clearance and non-infringement of deliverables
checks.description: A marketing agreement should require the Agency to clear all third-party rights in the deliverables and warrant non-infringement.

checks.name: Confidentiality of Client information
checks.description: A marketing agreement should require the Agency to keep the Client's non-public business information confidential.

checks.name: Subcontractor and influencer responsibility (flow-down)
checks.description: Where the Agency engages subcontractors or influencers, the agreement should make the Agency responsible for them and flow down its obligations.

types.name: Master Purchase Agreement (Goods)
types.summary: Master agreement for recurring purchases of goods under UCC Article 2, with releases or orders issued against it.

checks.name: F.O.B. point, title, and risk of loss
Inspection, rejection, and revocation of acceptance

types.name: Model / Talent Release
types.summary: Release of name, image, and likeness for commercial use, measured against state right-of-publicity statutes.

checks.name: Scope of media, territory, and duration
Irrevocability and waiver of inspection rights

types.name: Medical Director Agreement
types.summary: Medical directorship contract, the classic Stark/Anti-Kickback exposure, reviewed for the personal-services-arrangement conditions.

checks.name: Written, signed agreement with a one-year minimum term
Services specified and aggregate hours set in advance
Compensation set in advance at fair market value

types.name: Board / Shareholder Meeting Minutes
types.summary: Minutes of a directors' or shareholders' meeting, reviewed for the notice, quorum, vote, and adjournment record that makes the minutes evidence.

checks.name: Notice or waiver of notice recited

types.name: Membership Interest Purchase Agreement (LLC)
types.summary: Purchase of LLC membership interests, the LLC analog to a stock purchase agreement, with tax-treatment and 754-election terms.

checks.name: Operating-agreement consents and admission of the buyer

types.name: Merger Agreement
types.summary: Plan and agreement of merger under DGCL §§ 251–259.

checks.name: Material Adverse Effect (MAE) defined
checks.description: SPA must define Material Adverse Effect — central allocation-of-risk concept (Akorn / Channel Medsystems).

checks.name: Governing law and forum
checks.description: SPA must include governing-law and forum-selection clauses.

checks.name: Plan of merger / surviving corporation
checks.description: Merger agreement must identify the surviving corporation and the plan of merger (DGCL § 251).

checks.name: Merger consideration mechanics
checks.description: Merger agreement must specify the consideration mechanics — per-share consideration, treatment of equity awards, exchange agent.

checks.name: Appraisal rights notice (DGCL § 262)
checks.description: Stockholders must be advised of appraisal rights under DGCL § 262.

checks.name: Stockholder approval mechanism
checks.description: Merger agreement must address required stockholder approvals (DGCL § 251(c)).

checks.name: No-solicitation / fiduciary out covenant
checks.description: Public-company / target-board merger agreements need fiduciary-out language permitting board to respond to superior proposals.

checks.name: Termination fee / break-up fee
checks.description: Merger agreements typically include a break-up fee for fiduciary-out / superior-proposal scenarios.

checks.name: Drag-along / appraisal-waiver letter agreement reference
checks.description: Private-target mergers often pair with a stockholder consent / drag-along enforcement.

checks.name: Filing of certificate of merger (§ 251(c))
checks.description: Merger agreement should contemplate filing the certificate of merger with the Delaware Secretary of State.

checks.name: Treatment of options and RSUs at closing
checks.description: Merger consideration must specify treatment of in-the-money / out-of-the-money options and RSUs.

checks.name: Reverse vs forward / triangular structure stated
checks.description: Merger structure (forward, reverse, reverse-triangular) should be explicit.

types.name: MSA — Customer-Side Deep Analysis
types.summary: Deep analysis of a Master Services Agreement (or Master Subscription Agreement) from the customer's perspective. Oriented toward catching customer-unfriendly drafting: no security commitments, missing SLA, broad assignment rights, no data return on termination, indemnity carved out of the cap, sole-and-exclusive SLA credit remedy, missing wind-down period.

checks.name: Third-party IP infringement indemnity
checks.description: MSA must address third-party IP infringement indemnification.

checks.name: Indemnification procedure (notice / defense / settlement)
checks.description: Indemnification clause must include procedural mechanics (prompt notice, control of defense, settlement consent).

checks.name: Indemnity for breach of confidentiality
checks.description: MSA should indemnify for breach of confidentiality obligations.

checks.name: Indemnity for breach of data protection / gross negligence / wilful misconduct
checks.description: Indemnification must cover breach of data-protection obligations, gross negligence, or wilful misconduct.

checks.name: Indemnification carved out of liability cap
checks.description: Detects when indemnification is excluded from the aggregate liability cap.

checks.name: Aggregate liability cap present
checks.description: MSA must specify an aggregate liability cap.

checks.name: Liability cap carve-outs (fraud / wilful misconduct / IP indemnity)
checks.description: Liability cap must carve out fraud, wilful misconduct, IP indemnity, and breach of confidentiality.

checks.name: Consequential-damages waiver is mutual
checks.description: Consequential-damages waiver should apply to both parties symmetrically.

checks.name: California Civil Code § 1668 problem flag
checks.description: Flags a liability cap or exculpation that purports to limit liability for fraud, wilful injury, or violation of law where California law may govern — void per Cal. Civ. Code § 1668.

checks.name: New York Gen. Oblig. § 5-322.1 anti-indemnity flag
checks.description: Flags a broad indemnification for negligence in a construction-related MSA governed by New York law — void per N.Y. Gen. Oblig. § 5-322.1.

checks.name: Background / foreground IP allocation
checks.description: MSA must allocate ownership of background IP (pre-existing) and foreground IP (created during the engagement).

checks.name: Feedback license may be unbounded
checks.description: Flags a feedback license that conveys unrestricted, perpetual, irrevocable rights in customer feedback without scope limits.

checks.name: Workmanlike + conformance + no-malicious-code warranties
checks.description: MSA must include workmanlike-services / conformance-to-documentation / no-malicious-code warranties.

checks.name: Compliance-with-laws + non-infringement warranties
checks.description: MSA must include compliance-with-laws and non-infringement warranties.

checks.name: Implied-warranty disclaimer overreach (UCC alignment)
checks.description: Flags an implied-warranty disclaimer that may overreach the UCC's conspicuous-disclaimer requirement.

checks.name: SLA referenced or attached
checks.description: MSA must reference or attach an SLA where the service is hosted.

checks.name: SLA credit as sole-and-exclusive remedy
checks.description: Flags when service-level credit is stated as the sole and exclusive remedy.

checks.name: Termination for material breach
checks.description: MSA must include termination for material breach with cure period.

checks.name: Termination for bankruptcy / insolvency
checks.description: MSA must include termination on bankruptcy or insolvency.

checks.name: Wind-down period for hosted services
checks.description: Hosted-services MSA must include a transition / wind-down period on termination.

checks.name: Data return / portability on termination
checks.description: MSA must address data return or portability on termination.

checks.name: Force majeure is balanced (both parties)
checks.description: Force-majeure clause should apply to both parties symmetrically; payment obligations should be excluded.

checks.name: Assignment silent on change-of-control
checks.description: Flags an assignment clause silent on change-of-control / merger.

checks.name: Governing-law / venue jurisdiction mismatch
checks.description: Flags when the governing-law jurisdiction differs from the venue jurisdiction.

checks.name: Amendment-in-writing and no-waiver
checks.description: MSA must include amendment-in-writing and no-waiver clauses.

checks.name: Survival clause + entire agreement
checks.description: MSA must include a survival clause and an entire-agreement / integration clause.

checks.name: Order-of-precedence may bury operative terms
checks.description: Flags when an MSA's stated order of precedence places the MSA above its SOWs or Order Forms while operative terms (indemnity, liability, IP) appear to live in those subordinate documents.

checks.name: AI usage clause presence
checks.description: MSA should address whether the vendor uses AI / generative AI in providing the service.

checks.name: Texas anti-indemnity (Tex. Bus. & Com. Code Ch. 151) flag
checks.description: Flags an indemnity for the indemnitee's own negligence in a Texas-governed construction MSA — void per Tex. Bus. & Com. Code § 151.102.

checks.name: UCC § 2-719 limited-remedy fail-of-essential-purpose carve-out
checks.description: When a limited remedy is the exclusive remedy, the MSA should anchor the UCC § 2-719(2) escape if the remedy fails of its essential purpose.

types.name: Mutual NDA — Deep Analysis
types.summary: Mutual / two-way non-disclosure agreement under US trade-secret law. Checks cover DTSA whistleblower-immunity notice (18 U.S.C. § 1833(b)), Confidential-Information definition completeness, four standard exclusions (publicly available, prior knowledge, lawful third-party, independent development), permitted-use scope, residuals, return-or-destruction with attestation, injunctive relief with waiver-of-bond, governing-law viability, no-precedent / MFN, non-solicit carve-outs, no-license, authority representation, successors-and-assigns, plus the mutual-NDA symmetry check.

checks.name: DTSA whistleblower-immunity notice present
checks.description: NDAs with employees, contractors, or consultants must contain the DTSA notice of immunity for confidential disclosure of trade secrets to government or in court filings.

checks.name: DTSA notice substantively complete
checks.description: The DTSA notice must cover (a) immunity, (b) disclosure to a government official or attorney, and (c) sealed court filing — all three elements per § 1833(b).

checks.name: Confidentiality term clause present
checks.description: NDA must state how long confidentiality obligations endure — either a definite term, perpetual for trade secrets, or both.

checks.name: Trade-secret perpetual carve-out present
checks.description: Best practice: trade-secret obligations should continue for as long as the information qualifies as a trade secret, not be cut off by a fixed term.

checks.name: Confidential Information defined
checks.description: NDA must define 'Confidential Information' (or equivalent capitalized term).

checks.name: Exclusion: publicly available information
checks.description: The Confidential Information definition should exclude information that is or becomes publicly available through no breach.

checks.name: Exclusion: previously known to the recipient
checks.description: Confidential Information should exclude information already known to the receiving party prior to disclosure.

checks.name: Exclusion: third party lawfully obtained
checks.description: Confidential Information should exclude information lawfully received from a third party without breach.

checks.name: Exclusion: independently developed
checks.description: Confidential Information should exclude information independently developed by the receiver without reference to the Confidential Information.

checks.name: Residuals clause flagged for awareness
checks.description: Residuals clauses permit the receiver to use general knowledge retained in memory. Not inherently wrong but consequential for the discloser.

checks.name: Permitted-use scope is too broad
checks.description: Permitted use of Confidential Information should be limited to the specific Purpose; 'any business purpose' is overbroad.

checks.name: Permitted-use 'to evaluate the Purpose' framing present
checks.description: Best practice: a narrow 'to evaluate the Purpose' (or equivalent) framing of permitted use.

checks.name: Return-or-destruction clause present
checks.description: NDA should require return or destruction of Confidential Information upon request or termination.

checks.name: Return-or-destruction attestation requirement
checks.description: Return-or-destruction clauses should require a written certification or attestation of destruction.

checks.name: Injunctive-relief / irreparable-harm clause present
checks.description: NDA should acknowledge that breach causes irreparable harm and that injunctive relief is appropriate.

checks.name: Waiver-of-bond language present
checks.description: Best-practice NDAs waive the requirement to post a bond when seeking injunctive relief.

checks.name: Governing-law clause present
checks.description: NDA should specify the governing law of the agreement.

checks.name: Governing law from a viable jurisdiction
checks.description: Governing law should be chosen from a list of generally viable jurisdictions (Delaware, New York, California, Texas, England & Wales, Massachusetts, Illinois, Washington).

checks.name: No-precedent / no-MFN clause
checks.description: NDA may state that signing does not create most-favored-nation obligations or precedent for future terms.

checks.name: Non-solicitation lacks general-solicitation carve-out
checks.description: If a non-solicitation clause is present, it should carve out general solicitations not targeted at the other party's personnel.

checks.name: No-license / no-ownership-transfer clause
checks.description: NDA should state that disclosure does not transfer ownership or grant a license in the Confidential Information.

checks.name: Authority / no-conflicting-obligation representation
checks.description: NDA may include a representation that each party has authority to sign and that no conflicting obligations exist.

checks.name: Successors-and-assigns with consent
checks.description: Assignment should require consent and bind successors.

checks.name: Mutual NDA — symmetry: receiver-only obligation detected
checks.description: In a mutual NDA, obligations should bind both parties equally. Receiver-only phrasing breaks symmetry.

checks.name: Title commitment / title objections

checks.name: Closing conditions

checks.name: Risk of loss before closing
checks.description: PSA must address risk of loss before closing.

checks.name: Seller representations and warranties

checks.description: PSA should include broker / commission representations and indemnification.

types.name: Reg A+ Offering Circular
types.summary: Reg A+ Tier 1 / Tier 2 offering circular (Form 1-A) prose. Only the prose is checked.

checks.name: Tier 1 vs Tier 2 election + offering-size cap

checks.name: Form 1-A item structure followed
checks.description: Circular must follow Form 1-A item structure (Parts I / II / III).

checks.name: Risk factors specific to offering

checks.name: Use of proceeds + plan of distribution

checks.name: Investment limitation for non-accredited investors (Tier 2)

checks.name: Audited financials (Tier 2) — narrative reference

checks.name: Ongoing reporting (Tier 2) — Form 1-K / 1-SA / 1-U

types.summary: Relocation benefit and repayment agreement, reviewed for the repayment trigger, wage-deduction limits, and tax gross-up.

types.name: Remote Work Agreement
types.summary: Telework agreement, reviewed for the multi-state tax and wage exposure, expense reimbursement, and equipment/security terms.

types.name: Requests for Admission (FRCP 36)

types.name: Revocable Living Trust
types.summary: Revocable living trust under UTC + state trust codes with pour-over coordination. Execution formalities cannot be verified from text alone.

checks.name: Settlor / grantor / trustor identification
checks.description: Revocable living trust must identify settlor (also called grantor / trustor).

checks.name: Trustee + successor trustees
checks.description: Trust must identify the initial trustee and at least one successor trustee.

checks.name: Revocability / amendment power
checks.description: Revocable trust must clearly state it is revocable and amendable by the settlor.

checks.name: Funding — initial trust property identified
checks.description: Trust should identify initial trust property (often Schedule A).

checks.name: Distributions during settlor's life
checks.description: Trust must address distributions during settlor's lifetime (typically: all income and principal to settlor).

checks.name: Distributions on settlor's death — beneficiaries identified
checks.description: Trust must specify the disposition of trust property on settlor's death (named beneficiaries / shares).

checks.name: Pour-over reference (to coordinate with will)
checks.description: Revocable trust + pour-over will is a common pattern; trust should reference the pour-over will.

checks.name: Spendthrift + creditor-protection clause
checks.description: Trust should include a spendthrift clause restraining beneficiaries' creditors (UTC § 502).

checks.name: Execution formalities cannot be verified from text alone
checks.description: States on every trust, estate and family-law analysis that execution formalities (witnesses, notary, holographic and other state-specific requirements) cannot be verified from the document's text.

types.name: Revolving Credit Agreement
types.summary: Revolving credit facility on LSTA-style architecture, reviewed for the borrowing base, financial covenants, and benchmark-replacement terms.

checks.name: Interest rate, benchmark, and replacement waterfall
Events of default and cure rights
Waiver of non-waivable Article 9 debtor protections

types.name: ROFR / Co-Sale Agreement (NVCA)
types.summary: NVCA-style right of first refusal and co-sale agreement on transfers of common / founder stock.

checks.name: ROFR — company right
checks.description: Company should have a primary right of first refusal on third-party transfers.

checks.name: ROFR — investor secondary right
checks.description: Investors get a secondary ROFR to the extent the company does not exercise.

checks.name: Co-sale right
checks.description: Investors should have a co-sale right to participate pro rata in transfers above thresholds.

checks.name: Permitted transfers carve-outs
checks.description: Carve-outs for permitted family / estate-planning / affiliate transfers.

checks.name: Notice and election windows
checks.description: ROFR / co-sale need clear notice and election windows.

checks.name: Termination upon IPO
checks.description: ROFR / co-sale should terminate on IPO.

checks.name: DGCL § 202 noting requirement acknowledged
checks.description: Transfer restrictions must be noted on share records (DGCL § 202).

types.name: Records of Processing Activities (GDPR Art. 30)
types.summary: GDPR Art. 30 records of processing activities for controllers / processors.

checks.name: Controller / DPO identification — Art. 30(1)(a)
checks.description: ROPA must identify controller (and joint controller / representative / DPO).

checks.name: Purposes of processing — Art. 30(1)(b)
checks.description: ROPA must state the purposes of processing.

checks.name: Categories of data subjects and personal data — Art. 30(1)(c)
checks.description: ROPA must describe the categories of data subjects and the categories of personal data.

checks.name: Recipients — Art. 30(1)(d)
checks.description: ROPA must enumerate categories of recipients.

checks.name: International transfers — Art. 30(1)(e)
checks.description: ROPA must identify transfers to third countries with the safeguards in place.

checks.name: Retention periods and security measures — Art. 30(1)(f)–(g)
checks.description: ROPA must state retention periods (where possible) and a general description of Art. 32 security measures.

types.name: Restricted Stock Purchase Agreement
types.summary: Founder / early-employee restricted stock purchase agreement subject to vesting and a § 83(b) election.

checks.name: Purchase price stated
checks.description: RSPA must state purchase price (often par or de minimis).

checks.name: Vesting / repurchase right
checks.description: RSPA must specify vesting schedule and corresponding repurchase right.

checks.name: § 83(b) election advisory
checks.description: RSPA must include § 83(b) election advisory and 30-day deadline.

checks.name: Stock-power exhibit / escrow arrangement
checks.description: Repurchase right is typically enforced via stock power + escrow / book-entry restriction.

checks.name: Right of first refusal
checks.description: RSPA typically grants the company a ROFR on vested-share transfers (DGCL § 202).

checks.name: Lock-up / market stand-off
checks.description: Modern RSPAs include a 180-day IPO lock-up.

checks.name: Securities-law legend on certificates
checks.description: Restricted shares must bear Rule 144 / state-securities legends.

types.name: Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) Grant
types.summary: RSU grant under an equity-incentive plan (IRC § 409A short-term-deferral or deferred-compensation).

checks.name: Grant date and number of units
checks.description: RSU grant must state grant date and number of units.

checks.name: Vesting schedule for RSUs
checks.description: Standard 4-year vesting / 1-year cliff or similar.

checks.name: Settlement timing — § 409A short-term-deferral
checks.description: Settlement should occur within the § 409A short-term-deferral window (by 2.5 months after vest) or be a § 409A-compliant deferred-compensation plan.

checks.name: Tax-withholding mechanics
checks.description: RSU vesting triggers FICA / FIT withholding under § 3401.

checks.name: No § 83(b) for RSUs
checks.description: § 83(b) elections are not available for RSUs (no current property transfer); grant should make this clear.

checks.name: Termination of service — unvested units forfeited
checks.description: RSU grant should state that unvested units are forfeited on termination.

checks.name: Plan reference and conflict-resolution
checks.description: RSU agreement must reference its plan and provide a conflict rule.

types.name: Rule 26(f) Report and Discovery Plan

checks.name: Proposed discovery plan with the required subjects

types.name: S-1 Risk Factors (prose only)

checks.name: Risk-factor section heading + introduction
checks.description: Filing must include a clearly labeled 'Risk Factors' section with introduction (Item 105).

checks.name: Item 105 — material-risk-only standard + 15-page summary trigger
checks.description: Risk factors must address material risks only; > 15-page sections require a separate 2-page risk-factor summary.

checks.name: Generic / boilerplate risk factor flagged
checks.description: Risk factors must not be generic boilerplate applicable to any company.

checks.name: Hypothetical / 'could' risk-factor language flagged for specificity
checks.description: Risk factors that hedge as merely hypothetical without specifying current exposures should be flagged.

checks.name: Risk-factor headlines / subheadings (plain English)
checks.description: Each risk factor should have a concise, plain-English headline (Item 105 + Rule 421).

checks.name: Forward-looking statement safe-harbor cross-reference (PSLRA)
checks.description: Risk factors should cross-reference the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act safe harbor where applicable.

checks.name: Cybersecurity / data-breach risk factor
checks.description: Risk factors should address cybersecurity / data-breach risk (per 2023 cybersecurity disclosure rules).

checks.name: Climate / environmental risk factor (where material)
checks.description: Risk factors should address material climate / environmental / ESG risks where applicable.

checks.name: Prose only — financial statements and filing schemas are not checked
checks.description: States on every regulatory-filing analysis that Vaulytica checks only the drafter's prose — not financial statements, numbers, or filing schemas.

types.name: SaaS Agreement (Customer Side)
types.summary: Customer reviewing a SaaS subscription agreement. Watches for vendor-favorable risk allocation, weak SLAs, and aggressive auto-renewal. Based on Common Paper Cloud Service Agreement.

checks.name: Consumer anti-review gag clause
checks.description: Detects a consumer-contract term barring the consumer from posting negative reviews, ratings, or comments — void under the Consumer Review Fairness Act (15 U.S.C. § 45b).

types.name: SaaS Terms of Service (Consumer-Facing)
types.summary: Linter for a consumer-facing SaaS Terms of Service / Terms of Use. Checks cover cancellation parity under ROSCA (15 U.S.C. § 8403) and the state automatic-renewal laws. Dark-pattern checks also run (browsewrap, buried notice, class-action waiver, asymmetric jury-trial waiver) at elevated severity.

checks.name: Cancellation parity with signup (ROSCA / state ARLs)
checks.description: Consumer SaaS Terms of Service should let a subscriber cancel by a mechanism at least as simple as the one used to subscribe.

checks.name: Consumer anti-review gag clause
checks.description: Detects a consumer-contract term barring the consumer from posting negative reviews, ratings, or comments — void under the Consumer Review Fairness Act (15 U.S.C. § 45b).

sources.title: ROSCA, 15 U.S.C. § 8403, and the state automatic-renewal laws (the FTC's 2024 click-to-cancel amendments to 16 C.F.R. Part 425 were vacated in July 2025 and never took effect)

types.name: SaaS Agreement (Vendor Side)
types.summary: Vendor reviewing a SaaS subscription agreement. Watches for customer-favorable risk shifts, uncapped indemnity, and gold-plated SLAs. Based on Common Paper Cloud Service Agreement.

types.name: Simple Agreement for Future Equity (Y Combinator SAFE)
types.summary: Y Combinator SAFE (post-money or pre-money variant).

checks.name: SAFE identifies post-money vs pre-money variant
checks.description: Y Combinator publishes both post-money (2018+) and pre-money (legacy) SAFE templates; dilution mechanics differ materially.

checks.name: Conversion event defined (Equity Financing)
checks.description: SAFE must define the conversion event — typically the next preferred-stock financing above a threshold.

checks.name: Valuation cap or discount rate stated
checks.description: SAFE must specify at least one of: valuation cap, discount rate, or MFN.

checks.name: Liquidity event treatment
checks.description: SAFE must address acquisition / change of control before conversion.

checks.name: Dissolution event treatment
checks.description: SAFE must address treatment on dissolution.

checks.name: MFN provision references later instruments
checks.description: MFN should clearly attach to subsequent SAFEs or convertible securities of the company.

checks.name: Representations of the company and the investor
checks.description: SAFE should carry baseline representations of the company and accredited-investor representation of the investor (Reg D Rule 506).

checks.name: Interest-bearing SAFE language
checks.description: A SAFE is not a debt instrument; interest accrual is inconsistent with the YC SAFE form.

checks.name: Governing law and forum (Delaware)
checks.description: YC SAFE governing law is Delaware unless modified.

types.name: SBA 7(a) / 504 Loan Agreement
types.summary: SBA-guaranteed loan documents, reviewed against the SOP 50 10 program requirements including personal guaranties and use of proceeds.

checks.name: Waiver of non-waivable Article 9 debtor protections
checks.description: Detects a security agreement or finance lease purporting to waive the debtor protections U.C.C. § 9-602 makes non-waivable — notice of disposition, commercial reasonableness, the right to redeem, the deficiency calculation, or the breach-of-the-peace limit on self-help repossession.

types.name: EU Standard Contractual Clauses — Module 2 (Controller to Processor)
types.summary: Verifies the official EU SCC Module 2 text (Commission Implementing Decision 2021/914) is incorporated and checks Annexes I, II, III. Also runs the GDPR Article 28 checks because SCC Module 2 must satisfy Article 28(3) by reference.

checks.name: Subject-matter of processing identified
checks.description: DPA must identify the subject-matter of the processing.

checks.name: Duration of processing specified
checks.description: DPA must specify the duration of the processing.

checks.name: Nature and purpose of processing
checks.description: DPA must describe the nature and purpose of the processing.

checks.name: Type of personal data identified
checks.description: DPA must identify the type of personal data processed.

checks.name: Categories of data subjects identified
checks.description: DPA must identify the categories of data subjects.

checks.name: Obligations and rights of the controller stated
checks.description: DPA must state the obligations and rights of the controller.

checks.name: Processing only on documented instructions
checks.description: Processor must process personal data only on documented instructions from the controller.

checks.name: Confidentiality of authorised persons
checks.description: Persons authorised to process personal data must commit themselves to confidentiality.

checks.name: Article 32 security measures incorporated
checks.description: DPA must require the processor to take all measures required pursuant to Article 32.

checks.name: Subprocessor terms (Art. 28(2) and (4))
checks.description: DPA must respect the conditions for engaging another processor.

checks.name: Assist controller in responding to data-subject rights
checks.description: Processor must assist the controller in responding to data-subject rights requests.

checks.name: Assist controller with Articles 32–36 obligations
checks.description: Processor must assist the controller with Articles 32–36 obligations (security, breach, DPIA, prior consultation).

checks.name: Deletion or return at end of services
checks.description: Processor must, at the choice of the controller, delete or return all personal data after the end of the provision of services.

checks.name: Information available for compliance demonstration
checks.description: Processor must make available all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with Article 28.

checks.name: Subprocessor prior written authorisation (Art. 28(2))
checks.description: Processor must obtain prior specific or general written authorisation before engaging a subprocessor.

checks.name: Subprocessor change notification + objection right
checks.description: Where general authorisation is used, controller must be informed of intended changes and have the opportunity to object.

checks.name: Subprocessor flow-down of same obligations (Art. 28(4))
checks.description: Where the processor engages a subprocessor, the same data-protection obligations must be imposed on the subprocessor by contract.

checks.name: DPA in writing including electronic form
checks.description: DPA must be in writing, including in electronic form.

checks.name: Pseudonymisation / encryption referenced
checks.description: Art. 32(1)(a) lists pseudonymisation and encryption as appropriate measures where relevant.

checks.name: Confidentiality / integrity / availability / resilience
checks.description: Art. 32(1)(b) — ability to ensure ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems.

checks.name: Restore availability after incident
checks.description: Art. 32(1)(c) — ability to restore availability and access to personal data in a timely manner.

checks.name: Regular testing of measures
checks.description: Art. 32(1)(d) — process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating effectiveness.

checks.name: 'Appropriate measures' undefined hand-waving
checks.description: Flags DPAs that reference 'appropriate measures' without an Annex of technical and organisational measures.

checks.name: Processor breach notice to controller (Art. 33(2))
checks.description: Processor must notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.

checks.name: 'Without undue delay' present
checks.description: Breach-notification clause should include 'without undue delay'.

checks.name: Breach-notice content elements (Art. 33(3))
checks.description: Breach notification should include the Article 33(3) content elements (nature, categories, contact, consequences, measures).

checks.name: Breach notice timing stricter than 'undue delay'
checks.description: Flags fixed breach-notice deadlines that exceed regulator expectations (e.g., > 72 hours from controller awareness, > 5 days from processor awareness).

checks.name: Article 30 records of processing assistance
checks.description: Processor should assist controller with Art. 30 records of processing activities (RoPA).

checks.name: DPIA assistance (Art. 35)
checks.description: Processor should assist controller with Data Protection Impact Assessments under Art. 35.

checks.name: Article 27 EU representative referenced (where applicable)
checks.description: Non-EU processors should reference their EU representative under Art. 27.

checks.name: Article 37 DPO referenced (where applicable)
checks.description: Where required, the DPA should reference the Data Protection Officer under Art. 37.

checks.name: International transfer mechanism named
checks.description: Where international transfers occur, the DPA must name a Chapter V mechanism.

checks.name: EU SCCs incorporated by reference
checks.description: DPA should incorporate EU SCCs by reference where transfers require them.

checks.name: Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) referenced
checks.description: Following Schrems II, parties should reference a TIA where Chapter V transfers occur.

checks.name: Deletion-or-return choice belongs to processor
checks.description: Flags clauses where the processor (not the controller) chooses between deletion and return.

checks.name: Audit-substitution eliminates audit entirely
checks.description: Flags SOC 2 / ISO substitution that eliminates the controller's audit right rather than substituting it.

checks.name: Processor unilaterally amends instructions
checks.description: Flags clauses where the processor may deviate from controller instructions unilaterally.

checks.name: Personal data scope defined or annexed
checks.description: DPA should define personal data scope in an Annex (Annex I for SCCs).

checks.name: Technical and organisational measures annex
checks.description: DPA should include an Annex describing technical and organisational measures (Annex II for SCCs).

checks.name: Subprocessor list annex
checks.description: DPA should include a list of approved subprocessors (Annex III for SCCs Modules 2 & 3).

checks.name: GDPR-current terminology (Personal Data Breach defined)
checks.description: DPA should track GDPR terminology (Personal Data Breach, Data Subject, Processor, Controller).

checks.name: Controller / Processor roles named
checks.description: DPA should clearly identify which party is the Controller and which is the Processor.

checks.name: Signature block present
checks.description: DPA should be signed by an authorised representative of each party.

checks.name: Effective date present
checks.description: DPA should state an effective date.

checks.name: Term and termination clauses
checks.description: DPA should state its term and termination conditions.

checks.name: Governing-law clause present
checks.description: DPA should specify governing law (typically EU Member State or UK).

checks.name: Liability allocation
checks.description: DPA should allocate liability between Controller and Processor.

checks.name: Controller indemnifies Processor for GDPR fines
checks.description: Flags clauses where the controller indemnifies the processor for the processor's own GDPR liability.

checks.name: Processor caps audit cost on controller exclusively
checks.description: Flags clauses where the controller must bear the entire cost of any audit, including audits triggered by processor breach.

checks.name: Personal data referenced in document
checks.description: DPA should reference 'personal data'; absence likely means the wrong template.

checks.name: Notice clause present
checks.description: DPA should specify how formal notices (including breach notices) are delivered.

checks.name: Survival of GDPR obligations post-termination
checks.description: DPA should state that obligations applicable to retained personal data survive termination.

checks.name: Records of subprocessor changes available
checks.description: Processor should keep records of subprocessor changes available on request.

checks.name: Onward transfer obligations (SCC Clause 8.8)
checks.description: Where SCCs apply, the DPA should reference onward-transfer obligations per SCC Clause 8.8.

checks.name: Local-law disclosure obligations (Clause 14 / 15)
checks.description: Where SCCs apply, processor must notify controller of legally-binding requests by public authorities.

checks.name: SCC Clause 1 — Purpose and Scope present
checks.description: EU SCC Clause 1 (Purpose and Scope) must be present.

checks.name: SCC Clause 2 — Effect and Invariability present
checks.description: EU SCC Clause 2 (Effect and Invariability) must be present and unmodified.

checks.name: SCC clauses materially modified
checks.description: Flags any 'as modified' / 'notwithstanding' / 'as amended' language attached to SCC clauses — forbidden by Clause 2.

checks.name: SCC Clause 8 — Data Protection Safeguards
checks.description: SCC Module 2 Clause 8 (Data Protection Safeguards) must be present.

checks.name: SCC Clause 9 — Use of Sub-processors
checks.description: SCC Module 2 Clause 9 (Use of Sub-processors) must be present.

checks.name: SCC Clause 11 — Redress
checks.description: SCC Module 2 Clause 11 (Redress) must be present.

checks.name: SCC Clause 14 — Local Laws (TIA)
checks.description: SCC Clause 14 (Local laws and practices affecting compliance) must be present, anchoring the TIA.

checks.name: SCC Clause 15 — Public Authority Access
checks.description: SCC Clause 15 (Obligations of the data importer in case of public authority access) must be present.

checks.name: SCC Clause 16 — Non-Compliance with the Clauses
checks.description: SCC Clause 16 (Non-Compliance with the Clauses and Termination) must be present.

checks.name: SCC Clause 18 — Governing Law and Forum
checks.description: SCC Clause 18 (Governing Law / Choice of Forum and Jurisdiction) must be present.

checks.name: Adequacy: reliance on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework
checks.description: Flags reliance on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (or its UK extension) so the importer's certification and a fallback transfer mechanism are confirmed.

checks.name: Adequacy decision currency clause
checks.description: Where an adequacy decision is relied on, the DPA should anchor the reliance with a fallback for invalidation.

checks.name: TIA / Transfer Risk Assessment reference
checks.description: Where SCCs / IDTA cover transfers to a non-adequate country, the DPA must reference a TIA / TRA.

checks.name: Onward-transfer terms (Clause 8.7 / 8.8)
checks.description: Where SCCs apply, the DPA should address onward-transfer terms per SCC Clause 8.7 / 8.8.

checks.name: Exclusion: publicly available information
checks.description: The Confidential Information definition should exclude information that is or becomes publicly available through no breach.

checks.name: Exclusion: previously known to the recipient
checks.description: Confidential Information should exclude information already known to the receiving party prior to disclosure.

checks.name: Exclusion: third party lawfully obtained
checks.description: Confidential Information should exclude information lawfully received from a third party without breach.

checks.name: Exclusion: independently developed
checks.description: Confidential Information should exclude information independently developed by the receiver without reference to the Confidential Information.

checks.name: Residuals clause flagged for awareness
checks.description: Residuals clauses permit the receiver to use general knowledge retained in memory. Not inherently wrong but consequential for the discloser.

checks.name: Permitted-use scope is too broad
checks.description: Permitted use of Confidential Information should be limited to the specific Purpose; 'any business purpose' is overbroad.

checks.name: Permitted-use 'to evaluate the Purpose' framing present
checks.description: Best practice: a narrow 'to evaluate the Purpose' (or equivalent) framing of permitted use.

checks.name: Return-or-destruction clause present
checks.description: NDA should require return or destruction of Confidential Information upon request or termination.

checks.name: Return-or-destruction attestation requirement
checks.description: Return-or-destruction clauses should require a written certification or attestation of destruction.

checks.name: Injunctive-relief / irreparable-harm clause present
checks.description: NDA should acknowledge that breach causes irreparable harm and that injunctive relief is appropriate.

checks.name: Waiver-of-bond language present
checks.description: Best-practice NDAs waive the requirement to post a bond when seeking injunctive relief.

checks.name: Governing-law clause present
checks.description: NDA should specify the governing law of the agreement.

checks.name: Governing law from a viable jurisdiction
checks.description: Governing law should be chosen from a list of generally viable jurisdictions (Delaware, New York, California, Texas, England & Wales, Massachusetts, Illinois, Washington).

checks.name: No-precedent / no-MFN clause
checks.description: NDA may state that signing does not create most-favored-nation obligations or precedent for future terms.

checks.name: Non-solicitation lacks general-solicitation carve-out
checks.description: If a non-solicitation clause is present, it should carve out general solicitations not targeted at the other party's personnel.

checks.name: No-license / no-ownership-transfer clause
checks.description: NDA should state that disclosure does not transfer ownership or grant a license in the Confidential Information.

checks.name: Authority / no-conflicting-obligation representation
checks.description: NDA may include a representation that each party has authority to sign and that no conflicting obligations exist.

checks.name: Successors-and-assigns with consent
checks.description: Assignment should require consent and bind successors.

checks.name: Unilateral NDA — only discloser/receiver framing present
checks.description: In a unilateral NDA, exactly one party should bear the receiver obligations. Mutual / bilateral phrasing in a unilateral template signals a template mismatch.

types.name: Vendor Security Addendum
types.summary: Linter for a Vendor Security Addendum / Information Security Exhibit. Checks cover specific measures enumerated, security-review cadence, right-to-audit or SOC 2 substitution, incident-response notification window, vulnerability-disclosure handling, secure-development-lifecycle reference, data-classification mapping, named encryption standards, penetration-test cadence.

checks.name: Specific security measures listed
checks.description: Vendor Security Addendum must enumerate specific security measures rather than a generic 'industry-standard' hand-wave.

checks.name: Security-review cadence stated
checks.description: Vendor Security Addendum must state the cadence for security reviews / audits / certifications.

checks.name: Right-to-audit or SOC 2 substitution
checks.description: Vendor Security Addendum must provide a right-to-audit (customer-initiated) or a SOC 2 / ISO 27001 substitution clause.

checks.name: Incident-response notification window
checks.description: Vendor Security Addendum must specify a notification window for security incidents.

checks.name: Vulnerability-disclosure handling
checks.description: Vendor Security Addendum should state how it handles externally-reported vulnerabilities.

checks.name: Secure-development-lifecycle reference
checks.description: Vendor Security Addendum should reference a secure-development-lifecycle (SDLC) program.

checks.name: Data-classification mapping
checks.description: Vendor Security Addendum should state how Customer Data is classified and the controls that follow.

checks.name: Encryption standards named (FIPS 140-3 / AES-256)
checks.description: Vendor Security Addendum should name encryption standards (FIPS 140-3 / AES-256 / TLS 1.2+).

checks.name: Penetration-test cadence stated
checks.description: Vendor Security Addendum should state pen-test cadence.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — Security and Privacy Controls
FIPS 140-3 — Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules

types.name: Vendor Security Questionnaire (SIG / CAIQ)
types.summary: Vendor security questionnaire (SIG / CAIQ-style) with NIST CSF + ISO 27001 baseline.

checks.name: Information security policy / governance
checks.description: VSQ must confirm a written information security policy approved by management.

checks.name: Access control — role-based, least privilege, MFA
checks.description: VSQ must describe access control: RBAC, least privilege, MFA, and quarterly access reviews.

checks.name: Encryption at rest and in transit
checks.description: VSQ must confirm encryption at rest and in transit with stated algorithms.

checks.name: Audit / certifications — SOC 2 / ISO 27001
checks.description: VSQ must identify current third-party audits / certifications and provide a contact for report distribution.

checks.name: Vulnerability management + penetration testing
checks.description: VSQ must describe patch / vulnerability management cadence and annual third-party penetration testing.

checks.name: Incident response + breach notification SLA
checks.description: VSQ must describe the incident-response process and breach-notification SLA to customers.

checks.name: Subprocessor / fourth-party disclosure
checks.description: VSQ must list material subprocessors / fourth parties and their function.

checks.name: Election of directors covenant
checks.description: Voting agreement should bind stockholders to vote for the agreed board composition.

checks.name: Drag-along covenant
checks.description: Voting agreement typically carries the drag-along covenant requiring stockholders to support an approved sale.

checks.name: Irrevocable proxy
checks.description: Voting agreements typically grant an irrevocable proxy to back the voting covenant (DGCL § 212).

checks.name: Successor / transferee covenant
checks.description: Transferees of shares must agree to be bound by the voting agreement.

checks.name: Specific performance / equitable remedies
checks.description: Voting agreements should provide for specific performance / injunctive relief.

checks.name: Termination on IPO / sale
checks.description: Voting agreement should terminate on IPO or sale of the company.

checks.name: Stock-power-of-attorney for drag-along
checks.description: Drag-along enforcement is strengthened by a power-of-attorney in favor of the company / dragging party.

types.name: Whistleblower Policy
types.summary: Whistleblower policy under SOX § 806 + Dodd-Frank § 922 + SEC Rule 21F-17.

checks.name: Reporting channels — internal + external
checks.description: Policy must establish internal reporting channels and acknowledge external (SEC / CFTC / DOL) options.

checks.name: Non-retaliation prohibition + SOX / Dodd-Frank protections
checks.description: Policy must prohibit retaliation and reference SOX § 806 + Dodd-Frank § 922 protections.

checks.name: SEC Rule 21F-17 — no impeding whistleblower communications
checks.description: Policy must comply with SEC Rule 21F-17 (17 C.F.R. § 240.21F-17) — no provision shall impede whistleblower communications.

checks.name: Confidentiality + anonymous reporting
checks.description: Policy must offer confidentiality and an anonymous reporting option.

checks.name: Investigation procedure + corrective action
checks.description: Policy must describe investigation procedure and corrective action.

types.name: Work-for-Hire Agreement
types.summary: Work-made-for-hire agreement under 17 U.S.C. § 101 with backup assignment + DTSA notice.

checks.name: § 101 specially-commissioned-category recital
checks.description: Work-for-hire agreement must fall within one of the nine 17 U.S.C. § 101 categories for specially commissioned works.

checks.name: Backup assignment clause
checks.description: Work-for-hire agreement must include a backup assignment in case the work-for-hire designation fails.

checks.name: DTSA / 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b) notice
checks.description: Work-for-hire agreements with confidentiality obligations must include the DTSA whistleblower notice.

checks.name: Moral-rights waiver (where waivable)
checks.description: Work-for-hire agreement should address moral rights for works subject to VARA / foreign moral-rights regimes.

checks.name: Independent-contractor status + tax / benefits disclaimer
checks.description: Work-for-hire agreement (with non-employees) must recite independent-contractor status.

types.name: Written Consent in Lieu of Meeting
types.summary: Board or stockholder action by written consent.

checks.name: Written consent identifies the consenting body
checks.description: Consent must state whether it is from the board (DGCL § 141(f)) or stockholders (DGCL § 228).

checks.name: In-lieu-of-meeting recital
checks.description: The consent should recite that it is in lieu of a meeting (DGCL §§ 141(f), 228).

checks.name: Unanimous-consent statement (board consents only)
checks.description: DGCL § 141(f) board consents must be unanimous.

checks.name: Stockholder consent — minimum-vote threshold recital
checks.description: Stockholder consents must recite that the signing stockholders hold the requisite vote (DGCL § 228).

checks.name: Resolutions enumerated
checks.description: Consents should contain numbered or otherwise itemized resolutions.

checks.name: Notice to non-signing stockholders (DGCL § 228(e))
checks.description: Less-than-unanimous stockholder consents require prompt notice to non-signing stockholders.

checks.name: Effective date / dating
checks.description: Consent should be dated as of a specific date.

checks.name: Signature block on each consent page
checks.description: Each director / stockholder signing must sign — typically with a counterparts clause.
